Ghana’s path to the 2026 World Cup was one of the most impressive in the entire CAF qualifying campaign. Carlos Queiroz, the experienced Portuguese coach who previously managed Iran and Saudi Arabia at multiple World Cups, brought structure and tactical discipline to a squad that struggled for consistency in previous cycles. Eight wins from ten qualifying games, with Jordan Ayew contributing seven goals as captain, tells the story of a confident, cohesive unit. That qualifying form gives them real belief — even with Kudus missing.

Ghana vs Panama (June 17, Toronto) is Ghana’s most winnable fixture. Panama reached the World Cup as relative underdogs and have limited depth beyond their first XI. Ghana should be capable of winning this match if they apply their quality from the first whistle. Ghana to win at around 1.85-2.00 represents value. Both teams to score — NO at around 1.60 also appeals, given Ghana’s defensive discipline under Queiroz and Panama’s limited attacking threat.
[...]
For England vs Ghana (June 23), England are strong favourites. However, Ghana have historically been competitive against major European nations and with the right performance could steal a draw. Ghana +1.5 on the Asian handicap is the angle here — likely priced around 1.50-1.60 and reducing risk significantly. Ghana to score at least one goal (YES) also has appeal at around 1.55.
[...]
Ghana’s path to the round of 16 is possible but demanding. Beat Panama, take something from Croatia, and the expanded format’s third-place qualification route may be enough — even with a defeat to England in between. The Kudus absence is a genuine problem at a tournament level. However, Queiroz has built a resilient, experienced squad that knows how to defend and win collective battles.
[...]
Prediction: Ghana beat Panama, lose to England, and draw with Croatia. That leaves them on four points — enough to advance as a strong third-place side given the rest of the African group results. The Black Stars make it to the knockout rounds by the narrowest of margins. Stay across all the match previews and tips on our today’s free betting tips page throughout the tournament.

Ghana are the underdogs in a tough Group L containing England and Croatia. Progression to the knockout rounds — aided by the expanded 48-team format, where four best third-placed teams can advance — is a realistic target rather than a guarantee. Beating Panama looks essential, and a result against Croatia could prove decisive.
[...]
Expectations at home are tempered by the chaotic build-up and coaching change, but Ghanaian fans never lack ambition.
[...]
Under Carlos Queiroz, expect Ghana to be organised, compact and counter-attack-oriented — a defensively disciplined structure designed to frustrate stronger opponents and spring quick transitions through pacey forwards. Partey anchors the midfield, allowing the front players to break at speed. Ghana’s strengths are athleticism, directness and individual quality in attack; the challenge is balancing Queiroz’s pragmatism with the squad’s natural attacking instincts, and finding consistency after a disrupted build-up.
[...]
Attack: Genuine pace and goal threat through Ayew, Semenyo and Williams. Midfield: Partey is a top-class anchor, but creativity hinges on Kudus’s fitness. Defense: Athletic but prone to lapses; organisation under Queiroz is the key.
[...]
Goalkeeping: A question mark heading into the tournament. Depth: Solid in attack, thinner in defensive cover. Experience: Mixes seasoned

- Pace and power — Ghana’s forwards are among the most explosive in the tournament.
- Redemption story — the shadow of 2010 makes every Ghana run emotionally compelling.
- Star talent — Partey, Semenyo and (fitness permitting) Kudus can light up any match.
- Underdog energy — a passionate fanbase and giant-killing potential in a tough group.

Ghana face an uphill task in Group L with England and Croatia as clear favourites. A win over Panama is close to essential, and a positive result against Croatia could open a path to the knockout rounds via a best-third-place finish in the expanded format. The most likely outcome is a tight battle for third place. Projected: group-stage scrap for a best-third-place spot; knockout qualification possible but not probable.
